description:
Tool problems the run-4 blind sculptor (MESH-88) hit that are still open after the MESH-86 fixes. Its full list is /home/acw/Code/Ixdar/.claude/worktrees/mesh-88/tmp/frictions.md (stays in that worktree until MESH-88 lands or is archived).

1. sculpt-snapshot does not copy the .strokes sidecar beside each SVG, so the snapshot refuses to load ("skull.strokes is missing"). Hit in every round from 2 to 5; the sculptor copied it by hand. Copy every file the sculpt reads, sidecars included, and check the snapshot loads.
2. Stroke ids for shapes without a data-id are numbered by position within their group (MESH-86 bug 4 fix), so inserting a stroke mid-group renumbers every later one (zygomatic.2 became zygomatic.3). Give a new stroke an id that no later insertion changes (e.g. the next unused number in the group, recorded into the SVG by sync).
3. stroke-report's TOO STEEP check covers chains but misses fills: a bowl fill under the limit (radius 0.05, depth 0.21) still rippled. Extend the check to fills with the rule that actually predicts the ripples.
4. stroke-report says nothing when a stroke folds the surface through itself (deep socket fills at 0.30-0.35 rendered black inside-out patches); only the render showed it, costing two cycles per try. Report folded/inward faces per stroke. (Preventing the fold is MESH-78.)
5. A fill drawn in the Back view also moved underside vertices its camera sees almost edge-on, leaving a lumpy pit where nothing was drawn. Add a per-stroke (or node) limit on how edge-on a surface a stroke may move, or fall the weight off with the facing angle.
6. sculpt-sync's refusal for a point that misses the surface names cell-local pixels (735) while the SVG holds whole-sheet coordinates (3295); give the sheet coordinates too, and the stroke's id/group.
7. No tool puts a multiview cell next to the reference picture closest to it; the sculptor cropped and pasted every comparison by hand. Add a compare route/command (the Python CLI only calls it; images are composed in Java).
8. `ixd wt status <ticket>` printed another worktree's agent note (mesh-86's) as this worktree's last note (ai-workspace bug, not Ixdar).

Item 9 (base strokes from the reference pictures) moved to its own ticket on 2026-11-01.
definition-of-done: Items 1-7 fixed, each with a test (SculptSyncTest / StrokeSculptTest style, or test_cli for item 1); item 8 fixed in ai-workspace or split off. A snapshot of the run-4 round-5 sculpt made by sculpt-snapshot loads with no hand copying.
testing-plan: Run SculptSyncTest, StrokeSculptTest and ixdar_automation_cli tests; sculpt-snapshot the run-4 sculpt and load the snapshot; stroke-report on a deep socket fill and a back-view fill shows the new warnings.
changes-made: Items 1-7 fixed, tests in SculptSyncTest/StrokeSculptTest/test_cli SculptSnapshotTest. 1: sculpt-snapshot copies the .strokes sidecar beside each stroke_sculpt SVG and refuses a synced SVG with none; run-4 round-5 sculpt (archive/mesh-88) snapshotted to tmp/rounds/round01 and loads. 2: new stroke ids take the next number past every numbered id the group holds (never a position), and a shape with no data-pts keeps the data-id it carries, so a regenerated drawing names its own strokes. 3: TOO STEEP for fills uses the fill's real rim slope (union of sample bumps, FillStroke.rimSlope: ~2.1 x depth/radius at default spacing vs 1.54 for one bump) and a bowl's floor slope 2 x depth/inset; run 4's r0.05 d0.21 bowl is now flagged. 4: report marks FOLDS per stroke (faces its moves would turn inside out, how many the MESH-78 limiter held back, how many stay). 5: chain/fill moves fade from full at 60 deg from the stroke's camera axis to none at 75 deg (edge-on). 6: off-surface refusal names SVG sheet coords, cell pixel, stroke id and group. 7: new route/command reference-compare (cell | reference scaled to the cell's subject | 50/50 blend per row). Item 8 left for ai-workspace.

Item 9: route/command reference-strokes (ShadingEdges + ReferenceStrokes). Run 3's streaks: trace-reference --edges traced the outline of each unthinned edge band, so every edge became a closed loop of two parallel lines, unsigned and one strength; now Canny-thinned one-pixel lines linked end to end, ridge/valley from the light the rim shows, radius from edge width, depth from contrast under the terrace limit, fills radius >= sample spacing (smaller fills stippled), each mark kept only from the picture seeing the surface most squarely (no double counting). trace-reference --edges uses the same lines. Run-4 counts (ridges/valleys/fills; edges found): front 49/46/4 (273), 3/4 front-R 47/45/3 (172), 3/4 front-L 51/70/2 (211), right 0/95/3 (184), left 22/24/0 (138), back 0/46/5 (67), top 3/7/0 (132); 522 strokes.
